sources.title: MQP (Midland Quarry Products), The History of Cliffe Hill, company time line
sources.repository: MQP Ltd, company website, About, History. Read on 27 November 2026.
sources.note: Time line: 1870s, quarrying begins by Mr Jones and Mr Fitzmaurice of Birmingham; 1881, Jones and Fitzmaurice stop working Cliffe; 1891, J.R. Fitzmaurice acquired the quarry from his father and reopens Cliffe Hill, with Mr P. Preston as manager; 1894, the Cliffe Hill Granite Company was formed; 1896, the Cliffe Hill Mineral Railway begun; 1935, the company bought the freehold of the quarry from the original founder J R Fitzmaurice; 1949, the original founder Mr J.R. Fitzmaurice passed away; 1965, acquired by Tarmac Roadstone; 1989, Old Cliffe Hill Quarry closed after 98 years; 1997, part of the Tarmac and Hanson joint venture MQP; 2005, production resumed at Old Cliffe Hill. A company history, not a contemporary record. Ledger C0763 to C0768.

sources.title: Annette McGrath, The Rock Quarries of Charnwood Forest, Mercian Geologist, volume 16, part 4 (2006, published 2007), pages 241 to 260; Cliffe Hill Quarry at pages 253 to 254
sources.repository: East Midlands Geological Society, Mercian Geologist. PDF read on 27 November 2026. The Cliffe Hill account cites M. H. Billington, Cliffe Hill Mineral Railway, Leicestershire (Turntable Enterprises, Leeds, 1974).
sources.note: Page 253: Jones and Fitzmaurice, two businessmen from Birmingham, formed a partnership in the late 1870s to work the stone at Cliffe Hill for the small-scale production of setts and kerbs; the quarry closed after a few years and remained so for a decade, until Mr J. Rupert Fitzmaurice acquired the quarry from his father on 9 May 1891 (Billington, 1974); Peter Preston of the Enderby quarry was taken on as manager at 3 pounds a week; a licence to store and use explosives was obtained on 15 July 1891; the first load of stone was sold to a local farmer at 2s 6d a ton; on 1 November 1894 the Cliffe Hill Granite Company Ltd was formed; in 1896 a narrow gauge railway was built to the Leicester and Coalville line; the Bagnall locomotives were Cliffe, then Isabel and Rocket; the railway was used until 1947 to 1948. Page 254: the Rockside Company was set up in 1912 to sell the brown stone; the Fitzmaurice and Preston families jointly managed the company for 72 years, until Tarmac Quarry Products Ltd acquired it in 1965. Ledger C0763 to C0767.
